subject: chemistry
title: Using moles to balance equations
key_idea: (AQA: Higher tier) The balancing numbers in an equation are the mole ratio of the substances. Convert each mass to moles, divide by the smallest number of moles, and write the simplest whole-number ratio. Those numbers are the balancing numbers.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Experiments can show how many moles of each substance react. This section covers how to turn masses into balancing numbers.

items.text: Divide the mass in grams by the Ar or Mr.
This gives the ratio of moles.
If a number is not whole, multiply every number to make them whole, such as × 2 for 1.5.
Use the ratio as the balancing numbers in front of the formulae.

items: 4.48 g of iron reacts with 8.52 g of chlorine to form iron chloride.
Moles of Fe = 4.48 ÷ 56 = 0.08. Moles of Cl atoms = 8.52 ÷ 35.5 = 0.24.
Fe : Cl = 0.08 : 0.24 = 1 : 3, so the formula is FeCl₃.

blocks.label: The balanced equation
where: Chlorine is a molecule, Cl₂. 3 Cl atoms for every Fe means 3 Cl₂ for every 2 Fe.

items: Check whether the substance is an atom or a molecule. 0.24 mol of Cl **atoms** is 0.12 mol of Cl₂ **molecules**.
Fe : Cl₂ = 0.08 : 0.12 = 2 : 3 gives the same equation.

items: The simplest whole-number ratio of moles gives the balancing numbers.
Check whether each substance is atoms or molecules.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) A question may give two possible equations. Calculate the mole ratio from the data and see which equation matches.

items.text: 4.48 g of iron makes 24.84 g of lead. Ar: Fe = 56.0, Pb = 207.

items: State which equation it is, and show the calculation that proves it.
You can also work out the mass each equation predicts and see which matches the data.
Find the moles of two substances and compare them.
Match the ratio to an equation.
Always show the calculation and name the equation.

checks.q: 2.24 g of iron reacts with excess copper nitrate solution to form 3.81 g of copper. Calculate the moles of each. (Ar: Fe = 56.0, Cu = 63.5)
Use your answers to say what the ratio of Fe : Cu is. Which equation does it match: Fe + Cu(NO₃)₂ → Fe(NO₃)₂ + Cu or 2Fe + 3Cu(NO₃)₂ → 2Fe(NO₃)₃ + 3Cu?
checks.a: The ratio is 0.04 : 0.06 = 2 : 3, so it matches 2Fe + 3Cu(NO₃)₂ → 2Fe(NO₃)₃ + 3Cu.

checks.q: 0.12 mol of iron reacts with 0.16 mol of steam. What is the simplest mole ratio of Fe : H₂O?

worked_example.question:
Iron reacts with oxygen to produce an oxide of iron.

0.015 moles of iron reacts with 0.010 moles of oxygen gas (O₂).

Determine:
• the formula of the iron oxide produced
• the balanced symbol equation for the reaction.
answer_points: Ratio Fe : O₂ = 3 : 2, or Fe : O atoms = 3 : 4 (1)
worked_example.tip: Multiples of the equation are allowed.

worked_example.question:
Iron is more reactive than lead.

Iron reacts with lead nitrate solution to form solid lead.

Two possible balanced equations for the reaction are

Equation 1: Fe + Pb(NO₃)₂ → Fe(NO₃)₂ + Pb

Equation 2: 2Fe + 3Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2Fe(NO₃)₃ + 3Pb

In one experiment, it was found that 4.48 g of iron reacted with excess lead nitrate solution to form 24.84 g of lead.

Carry out a calculation, using the information above, to show which equation represents the reaction taking place.

(relative atomic masses: Fe = 56.0, Pb = 207)
worked_example.tip: A mass method also scores: equation 2 predicts 621 ÷ 112 × 4.48 = 24.84 g of lead.

worked_example.question:
Chromium metal, Cr, reacts with nickel sulfate solution, NiSO₄. Solid nickel is made.

Two possible equations for this reaction are:

Equation 1: Cr + NiSO₄ → CrSO₄ + Ni

Equation 2: 2Cr + 3NiSO₄ → Cr₂(SO₄)₃ + 3Ni

10.40 g of chromium metal reacts with excess nickel sulfate solution to make 17.61 g of nickel.

Deduce which equation, 1 or 2, represents the reaction which takes place.

Ar: Cr = 52.0, Ni = 58.7
answer_points: The ratio is 2 : 3, not 1 : 1, so equation 2
worked_example.tip: The last mark depends on correct reasoning from the two mole values.
